title: Restore torrent sessions and file selections after process restart
description:
Fork research: parallel GPT-6 Astra source reviews, 2026-10-25. Current application baseline: 3ae404b.

## Purpose and evidence

Simple Torrent restores cached torrents on startup. This application preserves handles/selections during in-process reconfiguration only; server startup creates a fresh empty engine. Persist unresolved magnets, metainfo, paused/running intent and selected files. Closed #36 removed a broken cache deletion path and did not implement durable sessions. Do not copy the fork cache under DownloadDirectory.

## Acceptance criteria

- Use a versioned private state store outside downloadable content, restrictive permissions, bounded parsing and atomic/recoverable updates. Keep private tracker credentials and raw source metadata out of synced public models and logs.
- Durably persist accepted additions, selections and user stop/remove intent, including unresolved metadata. A removed torrent must not reappear after restart. Bound saved entries and restoration work.
- Restore partial, paused, completed and metadata-pending torrents without duplicates or unintended starts; verify actual stored bytes instead of trusting stale completion counters. Respect outbound and admission policies during restore.
- Corrupt/partial state or an incompatible version must produce actionable errors and a safe recovery path, not a crash or uncontrolled downloads. Interrupted writes retain a valid previous state.
- Add process-level restart tests using local legal fixtures for pending magnets, partial transfer, subset selection, paused state and deletion; retain reconfiguration/deletion-reconciliation coverage.

## Scope

Implement within the existing Go engine, typed API, generated frontend models and authenticated handler chain. Use isolated legal fixtures; never test against live downloads. This is a new backlog item, not a claim that the proposed behavior already exists.
